cards.explanation: Nathan the prophet tells the king, "Go and do all that is in your heart…" (2 Samuel 7:3). That's a big yes for David's idea. It's the same kind of yes as "Take another cookie, friends, there's plenty."

The reason Nathan gives is "…for the LORD is with you." (2 Samuel 7:3). That's a true thing to say about David, and Nathan says it with a lot of confidence. I'd have said it too, and then I'd have checked the oven twice.

The answer is True. The LORD opens with a question: "Are you the one to build for Me a house to dwell in?" (2 Samuel 7:5). He starts with a question, not a list of orders. David came in with a plan and got a question back. I know that feeling from my own plans for a second batch.

The answer is False. God asks whether He ever said to any of the leaders, "Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?" (2 Samuel 7:7). The question points to a no. So the statement that He kept asking is False, because the text shows He never asked at all.

The answer is the pasture, following the flock. God says, "I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel." (2 Samuel 7:8). David went from following sheep to ruling a nation. That's a career jump you don't see on a resume every day.

The answer is a name like the greatest in the land. God says, "Now I will make for you a name like that of the greatest in the land." (2 Samuel 7:9). He doesn't just remind David of the past. He promises him something new. And you can't carve a name like that on a cookie stamper handle, friends, believe me, I've tried.

The answer is False. God promises, "No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning" (2 Samuel 7:10). He says He will provide a place so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. That's a big promise for people who've been pushed around.

The answer is house. The LORD says, "…He Himself will establish a house for you." (2 Samuel 7:11). David wanted to build God a house, and God says He'll build David one. And look at who's doing the building, it's "He Himself." David showed up with a cedar idea and got handed a bigger one.

The answer is a house for God's Name. God says of David's descendant, "He will build a house for My Name…" (2 Samuel 7:13). So God names the builder, and it's David's descendant. That's who gets the job.

The answer is for all time. God says, "…I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever." (2 Samuel 7:13). Forever, friends. Not a season, not a term. Some of my cookie boxes don't last till Thursday, so that word hits me hard.

The answer is True. God says, "I will be his Father, and he will be My son." (2 Samuel 7:14). That's a close family word, right in the middle of a promise about a kingdom. God says it about David's descendant.

The answer is False. God says, "But My loving devotion will never be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I removed from before you." (2 Samuel 7:15). Saul was the king before David. God sets Saul beside David's descendant, and the descendant gets the promise that stays.

The answer is by asking who he is to be brought this far. David opens with, "Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?" (2 Samuel 7:18). A king, and the first thing out of his mouth is a question about himself. I think that's a man who knows he didn't get here alone.

The answer is True. David prays, "And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, You have also spoken about the future of the house of Your servant." (2 Samuel 7:19). He's saying God didn't stop at bringing him this far. God also spoke about what's ahead for his house. I think David is still catching his breath.

The answer is that God knows His servant. David says, "What more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD." (2 Samuel 7:20). When God already knows you, you don't have to explain yourself. Me, I'd still try to explain for ten minutes, mustache waving the whole time.

The answer is False. David gives God the credit. He prays, "For the sake of Your word and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing…" (2 Samuel 7:21). The credit goes to God's word and God's heart. That's a humble thing for a king to say.

The answer is False. David says, "…there is none like You, and there is no God but You, according to everything we have heard with our own ears." (2 Samuel 7:22). He says it flat out. None like Him, and no other God.

The answer is nations and their gods. David says God performed great and awesome wonders "…by driving out nations and their gods from before Your people…" (2 Samuel 7:23). So the nations and their gods both went out. David is remembering how God moved ahead of Israel.

The answer is True. David says, "For You have established Your people Israel as Your very own forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God." (2 Samuel 7:24). He says it to the LORD directly. Israel belongs to God, and God is their God.

The answer is the LORD's name. David asks God to do as He promised, "…so that Your name will be magnified forever…" (2 Samuel 7:26). The name he wants lifted up is God's own. The king is asking for a big promise, and he points it at God's name.

The answer is that God revealed He would build him a house. David says God said, "I will build a house for you." (2 Samuel 7:27). Then he adds, "Therefore Your servant has found the courage to offer this prayer to You." When God makes the promise first, praying back gets a lot easier. It's like a friend texting "Door's open, just come in," and suddenly you're not worried about knocking.

The answer is that God's words are true. David says, "And now, O Lord GOD, You are God! Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant." (2 Samuel 7:28). Then he moves to his last request. He builds on what God said, and he says it's true.

The answer is bless. David asks, "Now therefore, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You." (2 Samuel 7:29). Bless is his ask. He's asking God to do what God already promised.
